pages.title: A small area change can alter a route
pages.text:
A small area change can alter a route
A narrow neck may contain few pixels.
Removing those pixels can disconnect the pocket
while changing total area only slightly.
Inspect the neck, top inlet, lower outlet and remaining wall boundary.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 6 / 19

pages.title: The spatial problem needs more information
pages.text:
The spatial problem needs more information
The top opening needs an inlet condition; the lower opening needs an outlet condition.
Walls, ﬂuid properties and momentum balance determine how a velocity ﬁeld can develop.
A mesh supplies locations for the calculation, not these laws.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 8 / 19

pages.title: A time-step condition
pages.text:
A time-step condition
For Cn ≥ 0, the explicit update stays nonnegative if
0 ≤ hQ/V ≤ 1.
A larger step can create a negative numerical concentration. The companion uses the
exact exponential, not this update.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 11 / 19

pages.title: Repeated removal gives an exponential
pages.text:
Repeated removal gives an exponential
Use n steps over time t:
Cn/C0 = (1 − Qt/(nV ))n.
As the steps become ﬁner,
C(t)/C0 = e−Qt/V .
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 12 / 19

pages.title: Two different tests
pages.text:
Two diﬀerent tests
Keep physics ﬁxed and reﬁne mesh and time step: compare a named output for numerical
sensitivity.
Compare that output with independent measurements: test the physical
model.
Neither comparison alone turns washout into a stroke prediction.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 19 / 19
